newsitem.title: SPAIN: Quake hits north Spain, Portugal, little damage.
newsitem.headline: Quake hits north Spain, Portugal, little damage.

text.p: A small earthquake struck the Spanish northwestern region of Galicia and northern Portugal in the early hours of Thursday with a maximum intensity of 4.8 on the Richter scale, police and civil protection officials said.
Despite being one of the strongest quakes to hit Spain in 10 years it caused only moderate damage, local police said.
"We had an awful night, packed with phone calls from scared people, but luckily at present we do not know of any injuries," a police official in Lugo told Reuters.
After the first shock at 2350 GMT, a series of aftershocks were recorded.
Local media said one person died of a heart attack after the quake, which was also felt in the northern regions of Asturia and Leon, Extremadura and in Madrid.
The epicentre was reported to be in the so-called "seismic triangle" of Triacastela, Becerrea and Sarria, in the province of Lugo, Galicia.
In northern Portugal, some people fled their houses after the quake shook buildings, but no injuries or damage to property were reported.
"People went into the street. But no one has referred any reports of damage to me," civil protection spokesman Joaquim Saraiva Coelho told Portugal's TSF radio.
